answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the protocol anchors identity verification to quadratic stake burning: deploying $k$ agents requires permanently destroying $O(k^2)$ tokens. When malicious agent volume attempts to swell like an incoming tide, this superlinear burn imposes prohibitive economic friction. Even at market liquidity's nadir, attackers face deterministic bankruptcy, ensuring a crystal clear economic guarantee where coordinated identity replication rapidly becomes mathematically impossible.
